newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bans "mixed" dances on television.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bans "mixed" dances on television.

text.p: Pakistan's new government ordered a ban on Wednesday on what it called "mixed" dances of men and women together on state-run television as part of its plans to promote Islamic culture.
An official statement said television officials were told at a meeting that the new government's priorities were different from those of the previous ones.
This appeared to be a reference to liberal trends introduced under former prime minister Benazir Bhutto to counter the popularity of foreign satellite channels.
"The present government wants to highlight Islamic culture and Eastern values," the statement said. "Mixed and lewd dance must be stopped," said the new 10-point television charter.
"Importance of blood relations and the strength of the family system must be stressed," it said.

"Through beautiful dramas and interviews, the nation should be informed about the harms of the broken family system in the West," it said. "Educative dramas should be shown (on television) to check the increasing trend for divorce among educated women."
